phase3_findings.description: scripts/implement-timeline.py composes the artifact name without the run-attempt suffix and passes it to `gh run download -n`, which matches exactly; every --run-id invocation misses, is classified expired, and exits 0 — AC4's retrievable-artifact clause is unreachable and the failure is success-shaped. The unit stub carries the same wrong name.

_artifact_name_prefix's name and the module docstring's 'downloads the run's execution-transcript artifact' claim are false against the uploaders' actual artifact name; the _EXPIRED_MARKERS comment reinforces the misreading by treating 'no artifact matching' as evidence of expiry.

AC10 unmet: docs/internal/improvement-loops/runtime-evaluations.md is not in the diff and documents none of the four added instruments (verified independently: zero occurrences of implement-timeline / implement-run-report / implement-benchmark / derive-run-profile).

AC1 fails whole-key: apply_run_profile_floor returns early on an empty DEVFLOW_RUN_PROFILE, so any of prepare-run-profile.sh's six warned no-profile branches leaves the record with no run_profile object at all — engine_outcome and prior_record_count, neither of which needs a workpad, are absent rather than recorded, and the workpad-sourced pair is absent rather than 'unestablished'.

AC4's per-step view is not rendered in the text channel: _render prints only 'Per-step records: N' plus an unestablished count, while the module docstring claims per-step output carries each call's duration. The data reaches --json only.

prior_record_count is documented (floor header and the changeset) as counting prior IMPLEMENT records for the same issue, but the pr-<N>-*/issue-<N>-* basename match counts every record-deriving command class's records under the same key, so review runs on the same PR inflate it.

implement-benchmark.py's module docstring states the verdict is withheld when a cohort holds fewer than MIN_COHORT_RUNS runs, while withholding_reasons gates on established_durations — an eight-run cohort with three established durations withholds, which the documented rule does not predict.

implement-timeline.py calls subprocess.run on the DEVFLOW_GH-resolved binary with no OSError guard; an absent or non-executable gh escapes as a raw traceback instead of the project's named remedy. Reproduced against HEAD. scripts/file-deferrals.py wraps the identical call for exactly this reason.

The --run-id arm reads the downloaded artifact bare while the --transcript arm wraps the same read in try/except OSError, so the same failure class is a one-line diagnostic on one path and a traceback on the other, with the temp path already gone.

prepare-run-profile.sh's `workpad.py body` arm sends stderr to /dev/null, collapsing auth failure, rate limit, 404 and JSON parse failure into one causeless warning — while every other arm in the same file preserves rc and stderr.

phase_durations_ms cannot represent a phase the parser never matched, so `complete` (len(established) == len(durations)) is True for a run measured on one phase — defeating the completeness flag exactly where it matters. Seed the map from PROGRESS_PHASES instead.

_TOP_LEVEL_RE transcribes the workpad row shape more narrowly than workpad.py's own _TOP_LEVEL_CHECKBOX_RE (no capital X tick, no `*` bullet), so those rows silently discard every timestamped note under them rather than reporting unestablished — in a module that deliberately imports the phase names to avoid this drift.

The retrospective's 'trailing 4-week' window is four POPULATED buckets, not four calendar weeks, so a sparse store renders a mean over months and draws regression baselines from arbitrarily old windows — in a human-facing weekly report.

telemetry-branch.sh's local-wins fallback warning names harness_cost/permission_denials/run_profile but _DEVFLOW_TELEMETRY_FLOOR_KEYS_JSON also holds issue_number and no_pr_reason — the two keys that make a PR-less run identifiable — so the operator-facing text understates what may be reverted.
prepare-run-profile.sh's header cites a CLAUDE.md inline-workflow-shell convention that CLAUDE.md does not carry; a maintainer sent there will not find the rule the file claims to obey.

Both workflows' 'Emitted by prepare-harness-floor.sh' comment heads a three-variable block whose third member, DEVFLOW_RUN_PROFILE, comes from the separate prepare-run-profile.sh glue — sending a reader tracing an empty profile to the wrong producer. Mirror defect in devflow.yml.

implement-timeline.py's PHASE_PREFIX comment says the trailing slash prevents a PREFIX match, but _phase_from_read uses path.find() — a substring search anywhere in the path. The guarantee is real; the wording names the wrong operation, and the substring reach is itself unguarded.

Several added comment blocks in the library/script population exceed the three-line prevention-only cap and carry derivation or provenance rather than the wrong change they prevent (the run-profile section banner, _prior_implement_record_count's docstring cost derivation, the apply_pr_less_issue_floor banner).

apply_run_profile_floor's merge arm (b) — attaching run_profile to a record already persisted on the telemetry branch for this run-id, the common cloud path — has no assertion at all, including its has("run_profile") no-op and its unreadable-blob continue.

_prior_implement_record_count is exercised only at its two sentinels (established 0, unestablished); the counting loop, the prefix match and the self-exclusion are untested, so an off-by-one that counts this run's own record would ship green.

The PROFILE_GLUE guard block, the DEVFLOW_ENGINE_OUTCOME env line and the four env passthroughs are a new byte-identical coupled mirror across devflow-implement.yml and devflow.yml with no assertion reconciling them; drift would leave devflow.yml's implement path silently profile-less.

_floor_merge_key_staged's already-carries-key and failed-merge arms, and the run-profile skeleton arm's pr-description / unknown-class gates, are unexercised — each produces the only breadcrumb evidence that a record lost a key.

implement-benchmark.py's three store-status arms and render()'s unestablished-mean withholding branch have no test, and download_transcript's run-missing / generic-failure paths stop at the classifier rather than being driven end to end.

is_reject is substring containment over free verdict text, so 'APPROVE (supersedes an earlier REJECT)' withholds a whole cohort; the repo's verdict identity is a producer-emitted APPROVE|REJECT token.

load_runs_with_status returns a stringly-typed union with an embedded payload re-parsed at four call sites, and both render functions default status="read", letting a caller assert a clean read it never performed.

run_profile has two independent producers (two fields from the deriver, five from the jq assembler), no schema_version and no shared key declaration; the nested issue_number is written and read by nobody.

The PR-less record is write-only in this diff: _collect_efficiency excludes any record carrying no_pr_reason from every PR's join, and load_runs reads only efficiency_runs, so no reporting surface can ever see a PR-less run's run_profile.

phase2_fails.evidence: grep over docs/internal/improvement-loops/runtime-evaluations.md for implement-timeline / implement-run-report / implement-benchmark / derive-run-profile returns 0 occurrences; the file is not in the diff. AC10's documentation half is unmet.

scripts/implement-timeline.py line 285 emits only `Per-step records: {len(timeline['steps'])}`; no per-step wall-clock total is rendered in the text channel, while the module docstring line 17 claims each step carries its duration. AC4's per-step clause is satisfied only in --json mode.

Both workflows upload `claude-execution-transcript-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}` (devflow-implement.yml:1821, devflow.yml:2470) while scripts/implement-timeline.py:90/108 composes `claude-execution-transcript-{run_id}` and passes it to `gh run download -n`, an exact-name filter. AC4's retrievable-artifact clause cannot hold.
